title: Tiered deprioritization runway and safe fallback rules for dependency/model/tenant guard rails
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: We need a deterministic, tenant-aware mechanism to move traffic off overloaded model dependencies with graded degradation rather than hard trips. Current per-tenant breakers are binary and cause sudden churn during regional spikes. This ticket defines a 'tiered deprioritization runway' (soft-deactivate → staggered-shed → fallback-chain) that maps to SLO tiers and multi-region failover behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Config schema supports three stages per entity: soft-deactivate, controlled-shed (pct-based), force-fallback
Per-tenant and per-model thresholds can be expressed as quantile windows (p95/p99) and error-rate windows
Runtime exposes metrics for stage transitions and decision rationale (reason tags) to Console
Automated canary dry-run for staged deprioritization passes with no customer-visible SLA regression in testbed
Docs and runbook published with playbook for manual override and rollback
implementation_details: Introduce DecisionState machine with states: NOMINAL, SOFT_DEACTIVATE, PCT_SHED, FORCE_FALLBACK, ISOLATED
Threshold inputs: rolling windows for latency quantiles (p50/p95/p99), error rate, backlog length, GPU queue depth
Hysteresis: require hold_duration (configurable, default 30s) plus cool_off (default 2m) before state changes revert
Soft-deactivate: change routing weight to 0.9→0.5 over runway_duration (configurable), enabling KV cache warming and token-prefetch to reduce cold starts
Pct-shed: probabilistic drop based on tenant priority vector (example: free=30%, standard=10%, enterprise=0%) with token-level reason header for observability
Force-fallback: deterministic routing to fallback model variants or regional endpoints with backlog-aware admission control
Fallback chaining: support prioritized fallbacks (model-small → model-quantized → remote-hosted) with TTL for progressive upgrade back
Config surfaces: API + Console UI for per-tenant policies and global defaults; YAML-backed central store with versioning and canary scopes
Decision export: trace/span annotated with decision.reason, decision.history, and confidence score for postmortem and ML calibration
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Dev/test: unit tests + local simulator; feature flag off in runtime
Phase 1 - Canary: enable for 5 internal tenants in us-west with dry-run flag (decisions logged but not executed) for 72h
Phase 2 - Shadow: probabilistic enforcement (1%) for canary tenants; monitor fallout metrics for 7 days
Phase 3 - Regional pilot: enable enforcement for low-risk customers in a single region with Ops on-call present
Phase 4 - Global opt-in: provide Console toggle to enable per-tenant policy; default remains conservative
Phase 5 - Default enable: flip default after monitoring thresholds validated and runbook rehearsed
testing_plan: Unit tests for DecisionState transitions covering edge cases and hysteresis windows
Integration tests using the load simulator that can inject latency spikes, queue saturation, and error bursts
Chaos test: simulate multi-region outage and validate fallback chain correctness and rate bounds
E2E testbed: create synthetic tenants (free/standard/enterprise) and assert observed shedding matches configured probabilities
Performance benchmark: measure added decision latency < 0.5ms p95 and no meaningful increase in token latency under normal load
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-region SLO alignment panel showing pre/post policy rollouts and delta in p95/p99
Alerts: spike in FORCE_FALLBACK transitions > 5/min for > 2m triggers PagerDuty
Healthcheck: automated smoke traffic after state changes to validate correctness; failures increment incident counter
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Incorrect thresholds cause excessive shedding for high-value customers. Mitigation: default enterprise exemption + dry-run telemetry before enforcement
Risk: Decision rules add tail latency. Mitigation: lightweight decision path in hot path and background reevaluation for low-priority flows
Risk: Fallback chaining leads to quality regressions. Mitigation: pair fallback config with model-quality tags and guardrail that blocks fallbacks that reduce quality beyond configured threshold
Risk: Cross-region cost explosion from failovers. Mitigation: cost budget checks and rate-limited cross-region spillover with explicit billing escalation
